title: Pinto Beans, canned, sodium added, drained and rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Pinto beans are a variety of dry legume popular in Mexican and Southwestern U.S. cuisine. In canned form they are typically cooked in a salty brine, then drained and rinsed to reduce added sodium. The beans have a creamy texture and a mild, slightly nutty flavor, making them convenient for salads, soups, and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “pinto” comes from the Spanish word for “painted,” referring to the speckled appearance of the dried beans.
Pinto beans are descended from the Mexican “frijol” that indigenous peoples cultivated over 5,000 years ago.
Canned pinto beans are a staple ingredient in chili con carne and classic Mexican fajitas.
Rinsing canned beans removes about 40 % of the added salt and some of the oligosaccharides that cause gas.
Pinto beans are a favorite protein source for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: A typical serving (≈130 g) provides about 7 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are essential for red‑blood‑cell formation and preventing anemia, especially in women of childbearing age.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Pinto beans raise blood glucose slowly, making them a good choice for people with pre‑diabetes or type‑2 diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in pinto beans help combat oxidative stress and inflammation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even after rinsing, canned beans retain a notable amount of salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Legumes can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people; additional soaking or enzyme supplements may help.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: A small percentage of the population may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rinsed pinto beans can be tossed into salads, added to soups, chili, stews, or used as a filling for burritos and tacos. They heat quickly on the stovetop or in the microwave with a splash of olive oil and your favorite spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened can in a cool, dry place. Once opened, transfer beans to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 4‑5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or mold.
